{{Short description|Quantity in a statistical analysis}}
An '''estimand''' is a [[quantity]] that is to be estimated in a [[Statistical inference|statistical analysis]].<ref name=":0">{{Cite journal|last1=Lundberg|first1=Ian|last2=Johnson|first2=Rebecca|last3=Stewart|first3=Brandon M.|date=2021|title=What Is Your Estimand? Defining the Target Quantity Connects Statistical Evidence to Theory|journal=American Sociological Review|language=en|volume=86|issue=3|pages=532–565|doi=10.1177/00031224211004187|s2cid=235405612 |issn=0003-1224}}</ref> The term is used to distinguish the target of [[Statistical inference|inference]] from the method used to obtain an approximation of this target (i.e., the [[estimator]]) and the specific value obtained from a given method and dataset (i.e., the [[estimate]]).<ref>{{cite book |last1=Mosteller |first1=F. |last2=Tukey |first2=J. W. |orig-date=1968 |chapter=Data Analysis, including Statistics |title=The Collected Works of John W. Tukey: Philosophy and Principles of Data Analysis 1965–1986 |volume=4 |publisher=CRC Press |year=1987 |isbn=0-534-05101-4 |pages=601–720 [p. 633] |chapter-url=https://books.google.com/books?id=C1guHWTlVVoC&pg=PA633 |via=[[Google Books]] }}</ref> For instance, a [[Normal distribution|normally distributed]] random variable <math>X</math> has two defining parameters, its [[mean]] <math>\mu</math> and [[variance]] <math>\sigma^{2}</math>. A variance estimator:

<math>s^{2} = \sum_{i=1}^{n} \left. \left( x_{i} - \bar{x} \right)^{2} \right/ (n-1)</math>,

yields an estimate of 7 for a data set <math>x = \left\{ 2, 3, 7 \right\}</math>; then <math>s^{2}</math> is called an estimator of <math>\sigma^{2}</math>, and <math>\sigma^{2}</math> is called the estimand.

==Definition==
In relation to an [[estimator]], an '''estimand''' is the outcome of different treatments{{what|reason=Is this supposed to be a medical treatment? Isn't this view too narrow?|date=June 2023}} of interest. It can formally be thought of as any quantity that is to be estimated in any type of experiment.<ref>{{cite journal |last1=Lawrance |first1=Rachael |last2=Degtyarev |first2=Evgeny |last3=Griffiths |first3=Philip |last4=Trask |first4=Peter |last5=Lau |first5=Helen |last6=D'Alessio |first6=Denise |last7=Griebsch |first7=Ingolf |last8=Wallenstein |first8=Gudrun |last9=Cocks |first9=Kim |last10=Rufibach |first10=Kaspar |title=What is an estimand & how does it relate to quantifying the effect of treatment on patient-reported quality of life outcomes in clinical trials? |journal=Journal of Patient-Reported Outcomes |publisher=Springer |page=68 |doi=10.1186/s41687-020-00218-5 |date=24 August 2020|volume=4 |issue=1 |pmid=32833083 |pmc=7445213 |doi-access=free }}</ref>{{what|reason=Why just experiments? Aren't there sampling situations that aren't experiments?|date=June 2023}}

== Overview ==
An estimand is closely linked to the purpose or objective of an analysis. It describes what is to be estimated based on the question of interest.<ref name="NASreport">{{cite book|last1=National Research Council|title=The Prevention and Treatment of Missing Data in Clinical Trials. Panel on Handling Missing Data in Clinical Trials. Committee on National Statistics, Division of Behavioral and Social Sciences and Education.|date=2010|publisher=The National Academies Press|location=Washington, DC}}</ref> This is in contrast to an [[estimator]], which defines the specific rule according to which the estimand is to be estimated. While the estimand will often be free of the specific assumptions e.g. regarding [[missing data]], such assumption will typically have to be made when defining the specific estimator. For this reason, it is logical to conduct [[Sensitivity analysis|sensitivity analyses]] using different estimators for the same estimand, in order to test the robustness of inference to different assumptions.<ref name="ICHdraft">{{cite book|last1=International Conference on Harmonisation of Technical Requirements for Registration of Pharmaceuticals for Human Use|title=Draft (final) concept paper on choosing appropriate estimands and definining sensitivity analyses in confirmatory clinical trials|date=2014}}</ref>

According to recent research, quantitative studies frequently fail to define their estimand.<ref name=":0" /><ref>{{cite journal |last1=Kahan |first1=Brennan |last2=Morris |first2=Tim |last3=White |first3=Ian |last4=Carpenter |first4=James |last5=Cro |first5=Suzie |title=Estimands in published protocols of randomised trials: urgent improvement needed. |journal=Trials |date=9 October 2021 |volume=22 |issue=686 |article-number=686 |doi=10.1186/s13063-021-05644-4 |pmid=34627347 |pmc=8500821 |doi-access=free }}</ref><ref>{{cite journal |last1=Cro |first1=Suzie |last2=Kahan |first2=Brennan |last3=Rehal |first3=Sunita |last4=Chis Ster |first4=Anca |last5=Carpenter |first5=James |last6=White |first6=Ian |last7=Cornelius |first7=Victoria |title=Evaluating how clear the questions being investigated in randomised trials are: systematic review of estimands |journal=BMJ |date=23 Aug 2022 |volume=378 |article-number=e070146 |doi=10.1136/bmj-2022-070146 |pmid=35998928 |pmc=9396446 }}</ref>  This is problematic because it is not possible for the reader to know whether the statistical procedures in a study are appropriate unless they know the estimand.<ref name=":0" />

== Examples ==
If our question of interest is whether instituting an intervention such as a vaccination campaign in a defined population in a country would reduce the number of deaths in that population in that country, then our estimand will be some measure of risk reduction (e.g. it could be a hazard ratio, or a risk ratio over one year) that would describe the effect of starting a vaccination campaign. We may have data from a clinical trial available to estimate the estimand. In judging the effect on the population level, we will have to reflect that some people may refuse to be vaccinated so that excluding from the analysis those in the clinical trial who refuse to be vaccinated may be inappropriate. Furthermore, we may not know the survival status of all those who were vaccinated, so that assumptions will have to be made in this regard in order to define an estimator.

One possible estimator for obtaining a specific estimate might be a [[hazard ratio]] based on a [[survival analysis]] that assumes a particular survival distribution conducted on all subjects to whom the intervention was offered, treating those who were [[lost to follow-up]] to be right-censored under random censorship. It might be that the trial population differs from the population, on which the vaccination campaign would be conducted, in which case this might also have to be taken into account. An alternative estimator used in a sensitivity analysis might assume that people, who were not followed for their vital status to the end of the trial, may be more likely to have died by a certain amount.

=== Epidemiological ===

In establishing clinical trials, often practitioners want to focus on measuring the effects of their treatments on a population of individuals. These aforementioned clinical settings are built with ideal scenarios, far removed from any [[intercurrent events]]. However, as this will often not be the case in reality, variability needs to be taken into account during the planning and execution of these trials.<ref>{{cite web |last1=Team |first1=Statistical Consultancy |title=Estimands – What you need to know |url=https://www.quanticate.com/blog/estimands-clinical-trials |website=www.quanticate.com |access-date=23 January 2021 |language=en-us}}</ref> By building foundational objectives around the idea of the estimand framework in clinical medicine, it allows practitioners "to align the clinical study objective with the study design, endpoint, and analysis to improve study planning and the interpretation of analysis."<ref>{{cite web |title=Estimand Framework: What is it and Why You Need it in Your Clinical Trial |url=https://www.ert.com/about-featured-news/estimand-framework-what-is-it-and-why-you-need-it-in-your-clinical-trial/ |website=ERT |access-date=23 January 2021 |date=4 March 2020 |archive-date=30 January 2021 |archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20210130205816/https://www.ert.com/about-featured-news/estimand-framework-what-is-it-and-why-you-need-it-in-your-clinical-trial/ |url-status=dead }}</ref> The estimand provides a way to explicitly state how these intercurrent events will be dealt with in achieving the objective of the treatment in question.

== ICH ==
On October 22, 2014, the [[International Council for Harmonisation of Technical Requirements for Pharmaceuticals for Human Use]] (ICH) produced a final concept paper titled ''Choosing Appropriate Estimands and Defining Sensitivity Analyses in Clinical Trials'' as an addendum to their E9 guidance.<ref>{{cite news |date=Oct 23, 2015| url= http://www.ich.org/fileadmin/Public_Web_Site/ICH_Products/Guidelines/Efficacy/E9/E9__R1__Final_Concept_Paper_October_23_2014.pdf | title= Choosing Appropriate Estimands and Defining Sensitivity Analyses in Clinical Trials | access-date= July 1, 2015}}</ref>
On 16 October 2017 ICH announced that it had published the draft addendum on defining appropriate estimands for a clinical trial/sensitivity analyses for consultation.<ref>{{cite news |date=Oct 16, 2017| url=http://www.ich.org/ichnews/press-releases/view/article/ich-releases-finalised-draft-guidelines-and-publishes-working-party-membership-for-first-time.html | title=ICH releases finalised, draft Guidelines and publishes working party membership for first time | access-date= July 6, 2018}}</ref><ref name="iche9r1step2">{{cite web |date=Jun 16, 2017| url=http://www.ich.org/fileadmin/Public_Web_Site/ICH_Products/Guidelines/Efficacy/E9/E9-R1EWG_Step2_Guideline_2017_0616.pdf | title=Estimands and Sensitivity Analysis in Clinical Trials E9(R1) Current Step 2 version | author=<!--Not stated--> | access-date= July 6, 2018}}</ref> The final addendum to the ICH E9 guidance was released on November 20, 2019.<ref>{{Cite web|url=https://database.ich.org/sites/default/files/E9-R1_Step4_Guideline_2019_1203.pdf|title=ICH E9 Addendum on Estimands|last=International Council for Harmonisation of Technical Requirements for Pharmaceuticals for Human Use|date=2019|website=ICH official website|access-date=December 12, 2019}}</ref> According to the addendum, there are five core attributes that comparise an estimand: (i) population; (ii) treatment conditions; (iii) endpoint; (iv) summary measure; (v) the strategies used to handle each type of intercurrent event in the treatment effect
definition. Kahan et al. provided tutorials on the ICH E9(R1) estimands framework.<ref>{{cite journal |last1=Kahan |first1=Brennan |last2=Hindley |first2=Joanna |last3=Edwards |first3=Mark |last4=Cro |first4=Suzie |last5=Morris |first5=Tim |title=The estimands framework: a primer on the ICH E9(R1) addendum |journal=BMJ |date=23 January 2024 |volume=384 |article-number=e076316 |doi=10.1136/bmj-2023-076316 |pmid=38262663 |pmc=10802140 |url=https://www.bmj.com/content/384/bmj-2023-076316}}</ref>

By providing a structured framework for translating the objectives of a [[clinical trial]] to a matching trial design, conduct and analysis ICH aims to improve discussions between pharmaceutical companies and regulators authorities on [[Drug development|drug development programs]]. The ultimate goal is to make sure that clinical trials provide clearly defined information on the effects of the studied medicines.<ref name="iche9r1step2" />
